Import CSV or TSV, select a table from extracted document text, choose the field meanings, review the complete output and compare the next source edition. The exported workspace uses the existing native merchant.

Project and native merchant

Imported route payment choices and metadata stay attached to their original resources. Use the merchant workspace to edit its complete ordered choices, then import its starter-input.json here.

Document table intake

Choose extracted HTML or Markdown containing tables, or reopen a retained document-table source. PDF extraction happens before this step. The complete extraction and selected cell origins travel with the project.

Original document details for a text file

These optional details are used when opening extracted text. Retained source JSON supplies its own complete document details.

Save or download the project to keep unfinished table choices. Open a preparations file with the extraction button.

Open an extraction to inspect its tables.

Numbers are the original table’s one-based rows and columns. Use comma-separated numbers or ranges. Omitted rows remain in the source; blank header rows produce Column N names.

Optional notes for explicitly excluded rows

Selected headers and data rows cannot also be excluded. Notes are optional for other omitted rows.

Select a cell to inspect its complete original text, markup and source coordinates. Covered cells show their anchor’s text here; the chosen merge policy controls the projected output.

Complete receiving

    
The ZIP contains native seller and workspace configuration, the mapped dataset, every original source edition, each saved mapping and reviewed output, full comparison files and the editable project. Extract it and follow its original merchant instructions. For another source edition, reopen source-tables/project.json.

    
The native dataset is a startup snapshot. Customer commissioning uses the existing source-bundle and workorder operation for the selected host, source rights, receiving application and release change.
